about.title: Dixon Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Dixon's economy runs on a mix of agriculture, logistics, and light industry, much of it clustered near I-80 and the rail corridors that cut through town. Workers here face real risks: forklift accidents in distribution centers, falls on farm equipment, repetitive strain from packing lines, and injuries tied to delivery vehicles moving along Rt 113 and West A Street. California generally requires injured workers to pursue workers' compensation through their employer rather than suing directly, but that's not always the end of the story. When a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to the accident, a separate third-party claim may be available alongside workers' comp benefits. LawProactive doesn't provide legal advice or represent you directly. We simply connect Dixon workers with an independent personal injury attorney who can review the details of what happened and explain what options might exist, all at no upfront cost to you.
commonInjuries: Falls from ladders, scaffolding, or loading docks

items.title: Third-Party Claims Beyond Workers' Comp
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against an employer, but if a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment maker contributed to your injury, a separate claim against that third party may still be possible.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: California law makes it illegal for an employer to punish you for reporting a workplace injury, so raising a concern shouldn't put your job at risk.

items.title: Awareness of Reporting Deadlines
items.desc: Workplace injuries generally need to be reported to your employer within 30 days, while a third-party injury claim carries its own separate two-year filing deadline.

items.question: I was hurt while making a delivery near I-80 in Dixon — does workers' comp cover that?
items.answer: If you were driving as part of your job duties, the injury is typically handled through your employer's workers' compensation coverage. However, if another driver caused the collision, you may also have a separate third-party claim against that driver. An independent attorney can help sort out which claims apply to your situation.

items.question: What happens if I don't report my injury to my employer right away?
items.answer: California generally expects injured workers to notify their employer within 30 days of the incident. Missing that window can complicate a workers' comp claim, so it's best to report as soon as possible, even if the injury seems minor at first.

items.question: Can I be fired for filing a workers' comp claim in Dixon?
items.answer: No, California law prohibits employer retaliation against workers who report injuries or file workers' comp claims. If you believe you've faced retaliation, that's a separate issue worth discussing with an attorney alongside your injury claim.
